domain_model: Each side uses the locked centerline plus locked left/right boundary as one continuous side membrane. No degree subdivisions, half-degree rings, fake shells, mask changes, or cap changes.
first_run_issues: Initial iterative bilinear per-cell renderer timed out in browser.
Second paired-boundary scalar pass also timed out.
Final artifact uses lightweight single-membrane side gradients to evaluate seam/body visual direction without changing geometry.
geometry_source: Phase 2.36f HTML DATA payload; centerline/leftBoundary/rightBoundary/polygon copied unchanged
goal: Eliminate visible primitive decomposition while strengthening near-ridge body mass and preserving continuous material edge integrity.
known_limitation: This is not the final local normalized shader. It is a visual-methodology prototype to test whether removing primitive decomposition and strengthening the near-ridge body improves perceived unity.
rendering_method: SVG side-membrane gradient prototype: one filled membrane per side plus carrier drawn last. No strip stack, quad boundaries, contour marks, laminations, cell skipping, noise, blur filter, or degree rings.

visual_assessment.first_run_issue: The lightweight membrane prototype reduces seams, but ASC exposes the limitation: the side membrane can read as a broad polygonal wedge rather than a final local pressure topology.
visual_assessment.risk: Because this uses side-level gradients, local normalized pressure is less exact than the desired final shader and can read as a side wedge in ASC. Use only for visual QA of unified body language.
visual_assessment.smallest_next_correction: If visually approved, implement the same unified-body language with a performant local normalized shader or precomputed raster/vector field; do not return to visible strip primitives.
